Figure out your total

Figure out your total

It comes down to three things: how many signatures, where we meet, and when. Pick yours and you’ll see the number.

1How many signatures get notarized?
$15 each · the most Colorado law allows

Every signature gets its own stamp. Two people signing one document = 2.

2Where do we meet?

Miles are counted round trip (there and back) from 5128 E Colfax Ave, Denver, CO 80220, my office at Tienda Salvadoreña.

    To count the miles, what you type goes to komoot’s OpenStreetMap address search (for the suggestions) and, if you don’t pick one, to the U.S. Census Bureau’s free address lookup. The map points go to OpenStreetMap’s route service. I don’t save your address. Data © OpenStreetMap contributors.

    Example: if you’re 15 miles from the store, that’s 30 miles round trip, so pick “A bit farther.” Travel is charged once per visit. Not sure? Pick your best guess and I’ll confirm it.

    Coordinating with your attorney abroad

    $50flat

    I email or WhatsApp your attorney to confirm how they want to receive the document, whether they need a translation, and where to send it. I don’t give legal advice; I follow the instructions your attorney gives you.

    Optional. For when your attorney in another country needs to receive the document.

    Why not ship it yourself?

    Walk-in counter rates for a single international envelope often run well above business rates. I ship at business rates, use a document envelope, and fill out the customs form with you. That saves you a trip and helps avoid customs delays.

    The fine print

    Rates are for standard document packets. Delivery times are carrier estimates and are not guaranteed. Customs duties or fees charged by the destination country, if any, are paid by the recipient. Shipping and courier fees are separate from notarial fees ($15 maximum per notarial act).

    8

    U.S. passport help

    Forms are free; I charge for typing

    I help you get your paperwork ready before you go to the federal office. I’m not a passport acceptance facility and I do not turn in applications for you.

    What the federal rules say

    • Appearance: First-time applicants (Form DS-11) must appear in person at an authorized passport acceptance facility or federal office. I cannot appear or sign in your place, and I cannot "drop off" or file your application for you.
    • Identity Verification: I do not verify your identity for the federal government; that is done by the Passport Acceptance Agent in person at the facility.
    • Government Fees: All U.S. Department of State and facility fees are set by the federal government and are paid separately and directly by the client. Passport forms (DS-11, DS-82) are free at travel.state.gov and you can fill them out yourself at no cost; my fee covers only typing and my time.
    Simplest

    Bilingual Form-Filling Help (Typing Only)

    $30per 30–60 min session

    Bring your own document or template. I type the answers you give me into the blanks and translate the form’s wording between English and Spanish. I do not choose the form or your answers, explain what a legal question means, or draft documents. If your document needs notarization, I can notarize your signature at the same appointment (the notary fee is separate).

    Note: This is a typing and translation service only. You decide what to write. For legal or immigration questions, please consult a licensed attorney.

    If the signing can’t happen

    If the signing can’t go ahead because of a missing ID, a signer who didn’t show, or another reason on the client’s side, the travel fee isn’t refunded, because it covers my time and mileage.

    Who decides whether your document is accepted

    What I charge covers my time, travel, and office work. I can’t promise that a court, agency, or anyone else will accept or approve your document. That’s up to whoever receives it.
